Seminar Title:

Processing, Microstructure and Fracture Behaviour of Biomimetic All-ceramics Composites with 4-Levels of Structural Hierarchy

Seminar Type:

Defence Seminar

Department:

Ceramic Engineering

Speaker Name:

Soumavo Sikder ( Rollno : 517cr1001)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Seminar Hall, Department of Ceramic Engineering

Date and Time:

20 Mar 2026 11.00 AM

Contact:

Arindam Paul

Abstract:

Bio-inspired nacre-like composites with lightweight and high toughness can be envisaged as next-generation high-performance structural composite materials, due to its unique &lsquobrick-and-mortar&rsquo architecture. This study explores the integration of two widely used ceramic materials Al₂O₃ (brick phase) and ZrO₂ (mortar phase) through an unconventional processing route involving freeze casting followed by single-step spark plasma sintering (SPS). The biomimetic alumina-zirconia (AZ) composites with 2 levels of structural hierarchy were consolidated (&gt98% dense) at 1300-1425 C with 50 MPa pressure. The hierarchical &lsquobrick-and-mortar&rsquo microstructure, akin to nacre, exhibited strength of 270 MPa, fracture toughness at crack initiation (KIC) and during stable crack growth (KJC) as 5.2 and 13.5 MPa&radicm respectively. The progressive failure of the bioinspired all-ceramic composites occurs by stable crack propagation with fracture energy almost 10 times higher than alumina (main constituents), an unusual and remarkable behaviour for a material exclusively composed of brittle constituents.

An exclusive strategy was employed to increase both strength and toughness of nacre-mimetic AZ composites by introducing SiO2-CaO liquid phase sintering aid (LP), to produce 3rd level of structural hierarchy. The addition of LP played a critical role in significant improvement of both strength and KIC to 470 MPa (~75% increment) and 6.7 MPa&radicm (~24% increment) respectively as compared to level-2 composites. Further, an additional level of structural hierarchy (level-4), similar to &lsquobrick-bridge-mortar&rsquo architecture of natural nacre, was created by incorporating submicron size alumina particles in the layered AZ-LP. This addition yields an extraordinary increase of KIC to 8.5 MPa&radicm (~30% increase than level-2). The strong interfaces between alumina platelets developed due the liquid-phase sintering aid (LP) and stress-induced phase transformation of tetragonal to monoclinic zirconia (denoted as intrinsic toughness) are attributing for remarkable strength and KIC for level-3 and 4 hierarchies. The positive influence of LP addition is offset by 25% reduction of KJC to 10 MPa&radicm, mainly due to less crack deflection (termed as extrinsic toughness) as layered interfaces disappeared between platelets. The intrinsic and extrinsic toughness are also uniquely isolated for each level of structural hierarchy. Finally, by optimizing the hierarchical architecture from micro to macroscopic level, the structural performance of the synthetic nacre is found to be superior to that of natural nacre and many other engineering materials (illustrated in the form of Ashby map).

Keywords: Bio-inspired composite, Al2O3 platelets, Zirconia, Brick-and-mortar microstructure, Structural hierarchy, Toughening mechanisms.
